title: mixOmics engine: tune_grid() fails with "incorrect number of dimensions" when predicting single-outcome PLS
description:
When using the mixOmics engine via plsmod with a single-outcome PLS model,
tune_grid() fails with the error:

``Caused by error in `tmp_pred[.x, ]`: incorrect number of dimensions``


This occurs because the internal helper multi_numeric_preds() collapses the prediction array to a vector when p = 1 and num_comp has length 1.

```
library(tidymodels)
library(plsmod)
library(mixOmics)

set.seed(1)
n <- 30
p <- 10
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n)
Y <- rnorm(n)
dat <- as.data.frame(cbind(Y, X))

rec <- recipe(Y ~ ., data = dat) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors())

pls_spec <- parsnip::pls(
                     mode = "regression",
                     num_comp = tune(), 
                    predictor_prop = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("mixOmics")

wf <- workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(rec) %>%
  add_model(pls_spec)

resamps <- vfold_cv(dat, v = 3)

grid <- grid_regular(num_comp(range = c(1L, 2L)),
                     predictor_prop(range = c(0.6, 1.0)),
                     levels = 2)

tune_grid(wf, resamples = resamps, grid = grid)

There were issues with some computations:

  - Error(s) x12: ℹ In index: 1. Caused by error in `tmp_pred[.x, ]`: ! incorrect number...

Run `show_notes(.Last.tune.result)` for more information.
Warning message:
All models failed. Run `show_notes(.Last.tune.result)` for more information. 

```

Cause

`In plsmod:::multi_numeric_preds() (file R/multi_predict.R):`
```
...
} else {
  new_nms <- ".pred"
  tmp_pred <- tmp_pred[, 1, ]   # <--- collapses 3D array to vector
  tmp_pred <- purrr::map(1:n, function(.x) data.frame(.pred = tmp_pred[.x, ]))
}
```
When `p = 1` and `length(comps) = 1`, this removes a dimension and causes the error.

Suggested fix
```
tmp_pred <- tmp_pred[, 1, , drop = FALSE]
tmp_pred <- purrr::map(1:n, function(.x) {
  data.frame(.pred = as.numeric(tmp_pred[.x, , , drop = FALSE]))
})
```
R version 4.5.1 (2025-06-13)
plsmod 1.0.0.9000
tune 2.0.0
parsnip 1.3.3
tidymodels 1.4.1
mixOmics 6.32.0

title: Feature request: Adding block.spls from mixOmics as a model
description:
Hello, and thankyou for maintaining this package! 

Just wanted to see whether there was any scope for adding block.spls from mixOmics as part of this package?

Not sure how feasible it would be to do this, I tried adding it as a new model following the guidelines but currently don't have the time/skill level/both to achieve this, but hope to keep working on it. I think the main issue is that block.spls takes a list of matrices as input, whereas the tidymodels workflow seems to expect a formula/matrix/recipe.

title: Feature request: Adding engine support for pls package?
description:
Hi tidymodels/plsmod devs,

First of all, thank you for creating and maintaining this package! I use PLS regression a lot for my work lately, so I'm really glad to have the option to write my analysis code in the tidymodels framework.

**I'm writing to ask if you would consider adding support for the [pls](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/pls/index.html) package as another engine?**

It implements some alternative PLS algorithms not included in the mixOmics package, including some that are standard in other software's PLS implementations. For example, it implements SIMPLS (De Jong 1993), which is the default algorithm used by Matlab's [plsregress](https://www.mathworks.com/help/stats/plsregress.html). (My supervisor is a Matlab native, so very selfishly I would love a tidymodels PLS engine that implements the same algorithm as Matlab so that we can double-check each others' work against each other's!)

- The main user-facing PLS function of the pls package, `plsr()`, takes formula syntax
- `plsr()` has a nice `predict()` method already set up that I think should be pretty smooth to fit into the tidymodels predict format
- `plsr()` also takes an `ncomp` argument, which could be set up as a tunable hyperparameter similar to how the mixOmics engine has it set up
- The package is also actively maintained so I feel safe that we would not be throwing users into a hole

One big thing that would require some work is the preprocessing function for the data. For multivariate predictors or responses, `pls::plsr()` expects all predictor and response columns to each be bound up in a single matrix-column. The `oliveoil` sample data in the pls package demonstrates what this looks like. For example, a multi-column X and Y PLS regression can be run with the following sample data from the package:

```r
library(pls)
oliveoil1 <- plsr(sensory ~ chemical, ncomp=1, data = oliveoil)
```

You can see that `oliveoil` is a 2-column dataframe, where `sensory` and `chemical` are both _matrix-columns._ Traditional multi-column dataframes can be converted into matrix-column dataframes doing something like:

```r
data(mtcars)
library(dplyr)

x <- mtcars %>%
  select(mpg, cyl, disp) %>%
  as.matrix()

y <- mtcars %>%
  select(hp, drat, wt, qsec) %>%
  as.matrix()

matrix_dataframe <- tibble(x = I(x), y = I(y))
```

I think it would be possible to use the role selector functions from the recipes package to pull the predictor and outcome columns out of a trained recipe and then preprocess them into matrix-columns for `plsr()`!

What do you think? Please let me know!

PS: I've never tried to implement my own parsnip engine before, but I see that there is a [tidymodels article](https://www.tidymodels.org/learn/develop/models/#add-an-engine) about it, so I can definitely try following that guide and contributing through a fork and pull request if that's of interest.

title: move model definition to parsnip
description:
We are standardizing to have our parsnip-adjacent package keep their model definitions in parsnip so that other packages can add engines. 

This package should take a version dependency of `parsnip >= 0.1.7.9000`.

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*
